transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-21
Time: 16:00 UTC (58 minutes)
Attendees: Jordan Ames (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Kai Moreno (Redwood CSM), Derek Lee (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Atlas - Head of ML), Tom Wu (Atlas - Infra), Sofia Beckett (Atlas - CTO), Marco Albright (Atlas - Security)

Summary (auto): Kickoff for Atlas MedTech onboarding to Redwood Private with VPC peering. Short list of security artifacts requested and pilot scope agreed: 2 inference endpoints for clinical note summarization, staging then prod ramp.

Topics: VPC setup, KMS/HSM expectations, SOC2 artifacts, runbook ownership, pilot timeline, resource sizing, routing and fallback.

00:00 Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone -- thanks for joining, we'll give folks a minute to come in. Hi Sofia, Lena, Tom, Marco, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya and Derek from our SE team and Kai from CS.
00:18 Sofia (Atlas): Hey all - thanks. We're excited to get started. We've got a lot stacked for Q2 so looking to make this as frictionless as possible.
00:24 Priya (Redwood): Great — quick agenda: run through current infra, clarify security/compliance needs, outline pilot success criteria, and map next steps and runbook owners. Sound good?
00:31 Lena: Yep that's perfect, we mostly want to make sure the data never leaves EU, and that keys are customer-managed.
00:37 Derek (Redwood): Noted. For Redwood Private we support KMS integration and customer-managed keys; we'll go through options for KMS, and we also have on-prem HSM hooks if needed — though that usually needs extra lead time.
00:49 Marco (Atlas): When you say "we support KMS integration" — is that direct through our AWS KMS CMKs or do you have a middle key store? We need to be explicit for audit.
00:58 Priya: Good question. For the VPC model we can be configured to use a customer KMS key for encrypting model caches and logs at rest; the control plane still needs to communicate metadata to Redwood but can be configured to leave payloads inside the VPC. We'll share the exact flow in the security pack.
01:15 Tom: To confirm, we run EKS in the eu-west-1 account, and our S3 buckets are locked down to that account. We need peering or private link, not open internet routes.
01:25 Jordan: That's the typical setup — we do VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink; pros/cons depend on your egress rules. We'll want the subnet IDs and SGs. Tom, can you share those?
01:34 Tom: Yes, we'll export the diagram. Marco will check compliance specifics.
01:39 Marco: Also want to map audit logging — specifically, can Redwood provide immutable audit logs for model inference requests and access?
01:47 Kai (Redwood CSM): We do — our platform can forward audit logs (or you can pull them via API). Default retention depends on plan, but we can provide logs to your SIEM via an S3 sink. We'll include the retention SLAs in the security pack.
01:58 Lena: For the pilot, success criteria: 1) P95 latency under 350ms for clinical summarization at 512 tokens, 2) zero data exfiltration incidents, 3) integration completed with our KMS, 4) monitoring and alerting wired to our PagerDuty.
02:12 Priya: OK that's a good crisp set. We'll run a baseline perf test in staging and share a perf spreadsheet. Note that latency will depend on model choice and quantization — do you have a preferred model?
02:23 Lena: We're testing an open clinical-tuned LLM (name withheld) and will likely need 8K context for some notes; can Redwood handle that sequence length in the Dedicated runtime?
02:33 Derek: Sequence length of 8K is supported but impacts memory and batch sizing. On Dedicated we can right-size GPU types; for Private we need to confirm instance types in your VPC or our managed nodes. We'll propose an instance profile.
02:47 Tom: On instance sizing — we prefer to keep compute in our account if possible, but we'd consider Redwood-managed nodes if that reduces ops burden. Thoughts?
02:55 Jordan: Two typical options: 1) Redwood runs managed nodes in your VPC (we still respect account boundaries and we can provision using an admin role), or 2) customer-managed nodes where we provide the helm chart and configs. Most customers choose managed nodes for faster ramp. We'll outline the ops tradeoffs in the runbook.
03:12 Sofia: Cost is a concern — we can't exceed our model inference budget. We need clear bucketing: per token + infra cost + storage. Is there an ROI calculator?
03:22 Kai: We'll provide a pilot estimate using your expected qps and model size — I'll attach a cost-sensitivity sheet. Also Redwood Optimize has recommendations for batching/quant that reduce unit cost.
03:33 Marco: We're regulated — SOC2 and ISO are must-haves. Do you have completed attestations and are those in the security pack?
03:40 Jordan: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts are available; we'll include the latest certs and the auditor contact. Also include our pen test summary.
03:50 Marco: Great. Also need to confirm retention windows for logs and ability to redact PII on request.
03:58 Priya: Redaction features exist in our pipeline; we can show a demo. For redaction at rest we can show tokenization or pre-filtering hooks.
04:10 Lena: Regarding fallback: If Dedicated nodes are saturated, what's the fallback strategy? We can't have interruptions for clinical workflows.
04:18 Derek: We support policy-based routing: canary fallback to a smaller hosted model variant (within constraints) or queue requests with SLOs. For clinical-critical flows, customers often set up an autoscale buffer in Dedicated to prevent saturation. We'll document recommended buffer sizes.
04:36 Tom: From networking side, how do we validate connectivity? Is there an agent?
04:41 Priya: We'll share a connectivity checklist — simple reachability tests, cross-account IAM role, sample curl for endpoint verification. We'll also coordinate a smoke test that runs post-peering.
04:52 Jordan: Actionable ask: Atlas to provide account numbers, VPC diagram, and list of subnets; Redwood to send security artifacts and runbook template.
05:02 Marco: On the runbook, we want explicit owner for incident steps, e.g., who toggles a canary rollback and who calls the on-call.
05:10 Kai: We'll include owner placeholders and suggested on-call rotations. You can replace with your RACI.
05:18 Lena: Can we set the pilot to a 2-week scope: week 1 staging perf and integration, week 2 limited production with 100 QPS and monitoring?
05:26 Jordan: That seems reasonable. We usually do a 14-day pilot for this kind of workload. We'll sketch milestones in a pilot plan doc.
05:33 Tom: Who will run the perf benchmarks? Redwood or Atlas?
05:36 Priya: We can run a co-owned benchmark: Redwood will run baseline tests, Atlas will run tests from your environment to measure network egress latency. We'll compare results.
05:45 Marco: For encryption in transit, do you support mTLS inside the VPC?
05:49 Derek: Yes, we support mTLS between services. We'll include cert rotation guidance.
05:56 Sofia: Any blockers from your side?
05:58 Jordan: Not blockers — mainly outstanding artifacts from Atlas. If you can get us the VPC details and compliance notes we'll be able to provision a staging environment and schedule the deep-dive.
06:07 Lena: We'll get those by Tuesday. Also, a small ask: can you provide an example of the monitoring dashboards we can expect?
06:14 Kai: I'll attach screenshots of latency, token breakdown, and per-route cost in the follow-up email.
06:20 Jordan: Okay let's capture next steps and owners, then do a quick recap.
06:25 Recap: Redwood to send security pack, runbook template, and perf spreadsheet; Atlas to share VPC diagram, AWS account IDs, and DLP requirements. Schedule deep-dive for 2025-03-26.
06:40 Sofia: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
06:42 Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with links.
06:46 End of meeting.

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-heard phrases (e.g., HSM sometimes transcribed as "H S M"), product names may be shortened in the audio. Shared artifacts referenced: security-pack_v1.pdf (will be shared), runbook-template-atlas.xlsx (will be shared), perf-estimate-template.csv (will be shared).
